item.title: Fat Bear Week is here: Meet Backpack, Bucky and other chunky contenders
item.description: Sixteen bears are facing off in Fat Bear Week​ 2026, the highly anticipated tournament among the chunkiest bears at the Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska.

item.title: Man shot by ICE being detained with bullet still in his back, lawyer says
item.description: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, the 28-year-old Venezuelan national shot by an ICE officer on Sunday, said in a phone call on Monday that he's "not doing well."

item.title: Man shot by ICE in custody with bullet lodged near his spine, lawyer says
item.description: In Austin, Texas, an ICE officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old Venezuelan man who, according to his lawyer, is now in federal custody with a bullet lodged in his spine. Jason Allen has video from the scene and more details.

item.title: Family tied to suspected Chinese spy gave $4.4M to Newsom, Calif. politicians
item.description: C.C. Yin's family has donated nearly $3 million to state-level California political causes and an additional $1,455,027 to federal campaigns.

item.title: Family tied to suspected Chinese spy gave $4.4M to Newsom, Calif. politicians
item.description: A California family gave over $4.4 million in political donations to Governor Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris and other leading California politicians. And now, that family's alleged past links to infamous suspected honeypot spy Fang Fang, also known as Christine Fang, and other Chinese government officials have thrust them into an ongoing debate over foreign influence in American politics.

item.title: Trump to address U.N. amid tensions with allies, war with Iran and Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: World leaders are in New York City this weekend for the United Nations General Assembly. President Trump is set to speak at the event on Tuesday. CBS News intelligence and national security reporter Olivia Gazis has more.

item.title: Trump meets with Mamdani ahead of U.N. address
item.description: President Trump started his New York trip on Monday with a visit to Gracie Mansion for a meeting with Mayor Zohran Mamdani. CBS News reporter Jared Ochacher has the details.

item.title: Converse apologizes for sneaker ad after critics say it uses racist imagery
item.description: American sneaker company Converse is apologizing for an ad campaign that critics say evokes racist imagery. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Videos show aftermath of Ukraine's massive attack on Moscow
item.description: Ukrainian forces launched a barrage of drone strikes against Moscow over the weekend in what the city's mayor called the largest attack on the Russian capital since the war began. These videos show the damage across the region.

item.title: When a trumpet player's trumpet failed him during the national anthem, he turned to his voice
item.description: During the national anthem at an Arizona Diamondbacks game over the weekend, the trumpet failed, but the trumpet player somehow turned immediately to a backup instrument - his voice.

item.title: AI, Iran likely to be on agenda for Trump's upcoming meeting with China's Xi Jinping
item.description: The Trump administration is gearing up for a planned summit in Washington with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. Craig Allen, former U.S. ambassador to Brunei, joins CBS News to preview the meeting.

item.title: Voting for Fat Bear Week begins Tuesday
item.description: Your annual chance to root for your favorite fat bears of Katmai National Park in Alaska begins on Tuesday.

item.title: Former "American Idol" contestant sobs in court, accused of killing his wife
item.description: A former "American Idol" contestant broke down in court on Monday as images and information about his ex-wife's execution-style killing were laid out in court. Tom Hanson has more details on the murder trial.

item.title: Paramount Skydance reaches antitrust deal with states over Warner Bros. Discovery purchase
item.description: Paramount's agreement with 12 state attorneys general paves the way for the company to complete its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

item.title: Bill Gates says it may take a catastrophe for the world to act on AI dangers
item.description: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates is in New York City this week for the UN General Assembly, hoping to prepare world leaders for the huge potential and huge threats AI poses. He spoke with Tony Dokoupil about his concerns.

item.title: Paramount Skydance reaches settlement with states over Warner Bros. merger
item.description: Paramount-Skydance has now settled two major lawsuits that were holding up the company's $111 billion buyout of Warner Bros. Discovery. One lawsuit was filed by the Writers Guild of America; the other by a dozen states. Paramount is the parent company of CBS News. Jo Ling Kent has the details.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's attorney requests investigation into holdout juror
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's lawyers asked a judge to question the holdout juror about his alleged use of a cellphone during deliberations and his truthfulness on a jury questionnaire.

item.title: Where things stand with 6 weeks until midterm elections
item.description: Just six weeks remain until the crucial midterm elections that could swing the balance of power in Congress. CBS News' Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's attorney asks judge to question holdout juror, review his phone records
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney is now asking the judge at her murder trial to question the holdout juror and review his phone records. Shanelle Kaul has more on that and an unseen part of the 60 Minutes Patrick Clancy interview.

item.title: Police officer wounded in shooting near synagogue on Yom Kippur
item.description: Police have not said what led to the shooting or whether the synagogue or Jewish community was targeted.

item.title: Police officer shot outside Ontario synagogue during Yom Kippur
item.description: The holiest day of the Jewish calendar, Yom Kippur, got off to a violent start just after sundown on Sunday night in Canada, when a gunman opened fire on a police officer outside a synagogue in Ontario. It's the latest in a string of synagogue attacks there this year. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue to restore White House access
item.description: The three news organizations, which were banned from White House grounds by President Trump, are arguing that the ban is unconstitutional.

item.title: No network TV coverage on Trump amid his unprecedented media ban
item.description: President Trump met with the New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday and was also preparing for Tuesday's UN General Assembly. But the president is also in the middle of a fight with the media, making it difficult to cover any of that as business as usual. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Thousands of flights canceled after FAA systems went down
item.description: More than 6,000 flights were canceled or delayed coast to coast because a construction crew accidentally severed a backup data cable from a radar facility near Philadelphia. The first line had already failed. Kris Van Cleave has more details.

item.title: Trump considered striking Houthi rebels in Yemen last weekend
item.description: Sources say President Trump nearly launched airstrikes against Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen over the weekend, but opted not to late Saturday. CBS News' Holly Williams and James LaPorta have more.

item.title: Banned news organizations sue Trump over press freedom
item.description: CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday announced a lawsuit over President Trump's White House ban against them, calling it a "blatant violation" of the first amendment. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe has more.

item.title: Flights to resume at NYC-area airports following equipment outage, FAA says
item.description: Flights at Newark Liberty International, John F. Kennedy International and LaGuardia airports were delayed due to an equipment outage, the FAA says.

item.title: Axios co-founder Jim VandeHei calls Trump's press ban "stupid, sad, terrible precedent"
item.description: Axios co-founder Jim VandeHei found a silver lining in the ongoing AI doom-and-gloom and co-wrote a modern survival guide called "Simplify: Do 50% More with 50% Less." Vandehei joins "The Takeout" to discuss the book, artificial intelligence and the Trump administration.

item.title: Massive East Coast air travel disruption caused by accidentally cut fiber line, Duffy says
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says an Amtrak crew accidentally cut into a Verizon fiber line in New Jersey on Monday, causing an outage that led to major air travel issues along the East Coast. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: No Trump TV pool coverage today after he bans 3 major news outlets
item.description: There will be no television pool coverage of President Trump on Monday after he banned three major news outlets from the White House. CBS News' Nancy Cordes explains.
